predecessors.note: The rebel zone is cut out of Cliopatria's Mexico: Mexico 1910 has 114 more cells than Mexico 1911. The page dates the first clashes to November 1910 (Treaty page: 'violent clashes began throughout Mexico in November 1910') but Cliopatria draws the zone for 1911 only, and the pages do not say where the rebels held ground in 1910.

land.text: the zone Cliopatria draws for the Maderistas in 1911, about Chihuahua City and the Guerrero district of Chihuahua; neither page names the land

successors.note: The zone returns to the federal state with the Treaty of Ciudad Juárez, signed 21 May 1911; Madero is elected president in October 1911 (Treaty page).

keyframe_review.note: unverified: both pages are silent on the land the Maderistas held. Cliopatria's zone is 34,589 km2 (114 cells, 27.5-29.4 N, 107.8-105.3 W: the Chihuahua City and Guerrero district of Chihuahua); the siege the Treaty page places at Ciudad Juárez (about 31.7 N) lies outside it and is carried as a contest zone instead. A faction has no infobox area to compare. The shape ends 21 May 1911 on the pages, not at the end of the year; the one-year step keeps it for 1911.

region.text: the zone Cliopatria draws for the Maderistas in 1911, about Chihuahua City and the Guerrero district of Chihuahua; neither page names the land

ledger.note: 1911: the Maderista rebels hold a zone in Chihuahua. Pages: 'violent clashes began throughout Mexico in November 1910' (Treaty page) and the Maderistas fought 'in 1910–11, during the first part of the war' (List of factions); neither names a place or a month, so the zone is Cliopatria's and the confidence 1. Counterpart carries the matching loss.

region.text: Ciudad Juárez, where 'in April the army began approaching' and the city 'was besieged by the end of the month'

ledger.note: April 1911: the Maderistas besiege Ciudad Juárez. 'in April the army began approaching Ciudad Juárez' and 'The city was besieged by the end of the month.' The page gives the month; the 40 km radius is the reading from the city name.

region.text: Ciudad Juárez, where 'in April the army began approaching' and the city 'was besieged by the end of the month'

ledger.note: 21 May 1911: the Treaty of Ciudad Juárez is signed, which ends the fighting at Ciudad Juárez. 'signed between the President of Mexico, Porfirio Díaz, and the revolutionary Francisco Madero on May 21, 1911.' The page gives the date of the treaty, not of the battle or of the siege's end; that the fighting there stops with it is the reading.

region.text: the zone Cliopatria draws for the Maderistas in 1911, about Chihuahua City and the Guerrero district of Chihuahua; neither page names the land

ledger.note: May 1911: the Maderista revolt ends and the zone returns to the federal state. The treaty was signed on 21 May 1911 and 'Díaz resigned on May 25, and interim president Francisco León de la Barra was the new incumbent'; Madero 'was elected president' in October 1911. The land is the zone the rebels held; the page does not name it.

wars.outcome: The Maderista rebels forced the Treaty of Ciudad Juárez on 21 May 1911; Díaz resigned on 25 May and Madero was elected president in October 1911.
wars.note: The first phase of the revolution only (Maderista revolt against Díaz, November 1910 to May 1911). The later phases belong to the mexico dossier.

certainty.note: A rebel-held zone with no treaty or survey line; the outline is Cliopatria's approximation of the ground the Maderistas held.

sources.title: List of factions in the Mexican Revolution
sources.note: Cliopatria's own link. Thin: 'Name given to various revolutionary armies fighting under the umbrella leadership of' Madero, 'in 1910–11, during the first part of the war'; no places, no dates of the uprising, no end.

sources.title: Treaty of Ciudad Juárez
sources.note: Clashes from November 1910, the April 1911 siege of Ciudad Juárez, the treaty of 21 May, Díaz's resignation on 25 May, Madero's election in October. Silent on the Plan of San Luis Potosí date and on rebel-held land in Chihuahua.

notes: BUDGET: two pages (List of factions; Treaty of Ciudad Juárez). NOT SETTLED: where the Maderistas held ground. Both pages are silent; Cliopatria's 114-cell zone (Chihuahua City and Guerrero district) stands unverified, and the sieged Ciudad Juárez is outside it. A gap-filler should open 'Mexican Revolution', 'Battle of Ciudad Juárez (1911)' and 'Pascual Orozco' for the Chihuahua fronts and dates (the mexico dossier cites 'Mexican Revolution' for the same year). START: the clashes began in November 1910 (Treaty page) but Cliopatria's row and the first dossier year are 1911; a 1910 keyframe was not possible from these pages. CAPITAL: none; neither page gives a seat of the rebel movement (capitals left empty). RULERS: omitted; the List of factions page names only Madero as the leader. The mexico dossier holds the loss (1911) and the gain (May 1911) with counterpart 'maderistas'. Region names used: place Ciudad Juárez, Cliopatria shapes; all in the gazetteer.
